*[Bug 18944] Add a preparsing filter step to aspell() in order to make LaTex spell checking more robust*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18944>

--- Comment #6 from Kurt Hornik (<mailto:Kurt.Hornik@wu.ac.at|Kurt.Hornik@wu.ac.at>) ---
Oh dear ... apparently I last worked on the new LaTeX aspell filter 2 years
ago.

Clearly, currently one cannot compose filters.  So to "enhance" an
available filter for pre or maybe also post processing one needs to
create a new filter wrapping around the available one, which is not
super-convenient as the available one are not directly accessible.  

That could be changed by exporting utils:::aspell_filter_db, which I
guess I should do in any case.

Currently,

R> names(utils:::aspell_filter_db)
[1] "LaTeX"        "Sweave+LaTeX" "md"           "Sweave"       "Rd"          
[6] "R"            "dcf"          "pot"     

where the first two are undocumented (and the second has a "Try to merge
into the Sweave filter." FIXME).  The unfortunately-still-undocumented
LaTeX filter wraps around utils:::aspell_filter_LaTeX_worker() which has

R> args(utils:::aspell_filter_LaTeX_worker)
function (x, cmds = NULL, envs = NULL, parser = tools::parseLatex, 
    ...) 

which I should document and say that one can also use the
parseLatex::parseLatex parser, which iirc these days handles errors
(more) gracefully.  (Need to re-run my test codes and discuss results
with Duncan.)

One could add a 'before' argument to the LaTeX filter/worker, and use as
something like

  if(is.function(before))
    x <- before(x)

before calling the parser on x.

Good enough ...?

*[Bug 18934] Improve computing of Kendall's tau in stats::cor()*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18934>

Martin Maechler (<mailto:maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch|maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch>) changed:

           What    |Removed                     |Added
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
     Ever confirmed|0                           |1
                 CC|                            |maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch
             Status|UNCONFIRMED                 |CONFIRMED

--- Comment #1 from Martin Maechler (<mailto:maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch|maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch>) ---
In the mean time, this has been taken up during R Dev Day / Rencontres R in
Nantes, June 19,  see  <https://github.com/r-devel/r-dev-day/issues/151>
initiated by a plan setup by Heather Turner, subsequently mentored by her and
me.
This resulted in working code, providing a patch:
  <https://github.com/r-devel/r-dev-day/issues/151#issuecomment-4756543031>

I've applied it to my sources and started testing, also compiled the C code
with more warning flags and with clang, and hence add some explicit casts etc.

Note that data with ties (in a column / vector) uses different code, so one
should test data with ties (as the `swiss` data) and without. 
I have done that now, not extensively, seeing that the computed results are the
same (only checking to default print() accuracy) and things work with NAs,
ties, etc, as previously.

I see that Heather has added this also for the R Dev Day in Warsaw next week,
but I will commit the current code and a NEWS entry, now...
which will leave more systematic tests for the R Dev Day (if desired).
